hash_source_note: All SHA-1 / CRC32 values were transcribed from MAME driver sources (mamedev/mame master): sinclair/spectrum.cpp, sinclair/spec128.cpp, sinclair/zx.cpp, commodore/c64.cpp, devices/bus/cbmiec/c1541.cpp, amstrad/amstrad.cpp, atari/atari400.cpp, acorn/bbcb.cpp. A null hash means no verified whole-chip hash is published; the chip is then identified through its bank entries. Phase 2: hashes for added machines were transcribed from the corresponding MAME drivers (fetched 2026-11-01). Combined 32KB hashes for the Spectrum 128/+2 were computed from the MAME-verified 16KB banks; the C64C 251913-01 bank split was verified by CRC32 composition. Phase 3: Dragon 64 package/sockets, Lynx and Archimedes socket numbering and the Jupiter Ace C1/D1 grid positions were confirmed against real boards (user-supplied). Commodore Amiga hashes: amiga/amiga.cpp.

backbit.chip: Original 23128 mask ROM (NEC D23128C / Hitachi HN613128P) - no native 23128 setting: read as 27128 with Pin 27 tied to +5V
backbit.warning: Use an interposer socket to tie Pin 27 to Pin 28 (+5V). Sinclair 23128 mask ROMs use Pin 27 as an active-high CS2, whereas the BackBit 27128 setting expects it to be /PGM. Failing to pull Pin 27 high will result in a blank read.

backbit.chip: 27C128 / 27C256 EPROM (a later replacement on a modified board - 48K machines left the factory with a mask ROM)

roms.replacement: 27C128 (16KB) or 27C256 (32KB) EPROM - not a drop-in swap: the board must be modified first. Link pin 1 to pin 28 (+5V). Remove the ROM select links and drive EPROM pin 20 from an OR of /ROM_CS and /MREQ (two Schottky diodes such as BAT85 and a 10K resistor). Tie pin 27 to +5V for a 27C128; on a 27C256 pin 27 is A14 and selects the lower (GND) or upper (+5V) 16KB, so burn the image into both halves, or fit a switch to choose between two ROMs. Guide: https://blog.retroleum.co.uk/electronics-articles/how-to-replace-the-rom-of-a-zx-spectrum-with-an-eprom/
warnings: A 48K board fitted with an EPROM has been modified (pin 1 linked to pin 28, an OR gate on pin 20, pin 27 tied high or switched). Check those changes before trusting a dump or fitting a different chip. If pin 20 was wired straight to /ROM_CS without the /MREQ OR gate, programs that read port $FE misbehave - e.g. Zynaps starts on its own during the title tune.

The BackBit has no 23128 setting. An original Sinclair mask ROM is read with the 27128 setting through a Pin 27 -> Pin 28 (+5V) interposer (see the Hardware / Polarity Warning); a genuine 27128 EPROM is read with the 27128 setting directly, without the interposer. Check which chip is fitted (quartz window / part number) first.
notes: EPROM replacement modifications: https://blog.retroleum.co.uk/electronics-articles/how-to-replace-the-rom-of-a-zx-spectrum-with-an-eprom/

roms.name: Character Generator ROM
roms.description: C64 character set (upper/graphics + lower/upper case), read by the VIC-II.
roms.replacement: 2732 / 27C32 on a 2332 adapter, or a 2764/27C64 on an adapter holding the character set (often with an alternate set in the other half).
warnings: CRITICAL - 2332 chip-select polarity: the 2332 is a 24-pin mask ROM with TWO mask-programmed chip selects. On the C64 character ROM CS1 (pin 20) is active LOW and CS2 (pin 21) is active HIGH. A 2532 or 2732 EPROM has a different pinout (pin 21 is A11 / VPP, pin 20 is /OE) and will not work in this socket without an adapter.
Use the 2332 setting so the tester drives CS2 high. With the wrong polarity the chip stays disabled and the dump reads as all FF or floating-bus noise.
notes: A corrupted character ROM shows as garbled or missing characters on an otherwise working READY screen.
